title: Chapter 2729: Revisiting Heavenly White Valley(End of Gaia’s Heaven Arc)
content:
Chapter 2729: Revisiting Heavenly White Valley(End of Gaia’s Heaven Arc)

"Mu Xuelian? What are you doing here? No... where am I?" Yuan muttered, his memories feeling somewhat hazy.

"You... don’t remember?" Mu Xuelian raised an eyebrow at him.

Yuan fell silent for a moment as his memories slowly cleared.

"Ah... I see... I have returned to the Nine Heavens..."

"What are you talking about? You never left," Mu Xuelian said after hearing his mumbling.

Yuan wasn’t surprised by her words, since he already knew he’d traveled to Gaia’s Heaven only with his soul, not his physical body.

"How long have I been asleep?" Yuan then asked.

"Three days."

"T-Three days?!" Yuan exclaimed in shock.

He had experienced several years in the other world, yet only three days had passed in the Nine Heavens. The difference in the flow of time between the two worlds was far greater than he had expected.

This realization immediately worried Yuan, especially since the other world was already on the verge of a full-scale invasion.

Although the Eternal gave them more time by strengthening the barrier, it wasn’t a permanent solution.

However, even if Yuan wanted to return to the other world, he wasn’t sure how.

He looked around the chamber, but it was completely empty.

’Not even a clue, huh?’ Yuan sighed inwardly.

"So, what did you acquire in here?" Mu Xuelian asked.

"What do you mean?" When Yuan turned to look at her, he realized that Shiva had taken her place and was the one who had just spoken.

"Are you really going to act dumb?"

Shiva flipped her right palm, conjuring an ice mirror before Yuan and said, "Take a look at yourself."

Yuan looked into the mirror, and his eyes widened slightly. Although most of the otherworldly changes he had undergone in Gaia’s Heaven had reverted, they hadn’t disappeared completely.

A noticeable strand of white hair remained among his otherwise black hair, while his right eye still shimmered with a myriad of colors.

"Not only that, but your aura..." Shiva narrowed her eyes before asking in a somewhat nervous tone, "How much Eternal Essence can you wield right now?"

Although she couldn’t tell exactly how much stronger Yuan had become, the natural presence he exuded made it obvious that his strength had increased drastically.

’For his aura to have grown so much in such a short time... whatever he acquired in this place is definitely extraordinary!’ Shiva thought to herself.

"I didn’t acquire anything in here," Yuan said, not bothering to reveal the truth to her.

"Is that so?" Shiva didn’t press him further, knowing he still didn’t fully trust her.

"In any case, are we done here?" she then asked.

"Yes."

Yuan stretched his body a bit before leaving the chamber.

On his way out, Yuan examined his body and its condition.

’As I thought, the cultivation I gained in the other world didn’t transfer to this body... However, my Eternal Essence is a different story.’

Although his cultivation remained at the God Ascension realm, all of the Eternal Essence he had accumulated in the other world had carried over, meaning he still possessed ten trillion years’ worth of Eternal Essence.

While it was a pity that his cultivation hadn’t increased, it hardly mattered in the grand scheme of things. What truly mattered was the growth of his Eternal Essence, since ordinary cultivation had little effect against Eternals.

Of course, Gaia’s System also remained.

Once they returned to the surface, Mu Xuelian asked, "Where are we going now?"

"I’m going to complete my physique, but first..."

Yuan turned to look in the direction of the Heavenly White Valley and mumbled, "Since I’m already here, I might as well check up on them."

Some time later, Yuan arrived at the Heavenly White Valley. However, upon seeing the state it was in, he could hardly comprehend what lay before his eyes.

"What the fuck happened here?" Yuan couldn’t help but curse aloud as he stared at the scorched land before him, as if a massive wildfire had recently swept through and consumed everything in its path.

Not only had the entire Heavenly White Valley been destroyed, but there wasn’t a single sign of life remaining.

After snapping out of his daze, Yuan searched the area for any clues that might explain what had happened.

However, with the entire place reduced to ruins, he had little hope of finding anything useful.

Eventually, Yuan reached the main residential area where the Clan Leader and elders had lived, only to find it, too, had been completely destroyed.

The first person who came to Yuan’s mind upon seeing the devastation was a certain little girl.

’What in heaven’s name happened here? Bai Sulan... I hope nothing happened to her.’

After confirming nothing remained, Yuan made his way to the last place left—the Heavenly White Tiger’s Ancestral Altar.

Upon arriving, Yuan immediately noticed that the gates were wide open.

Although their ancestor’s blood essence was no longer there, the Heavenly White Tiger Clan had chosen to continue treating the place as sacred, guarding it just as strictly as before. Under normal circumstances, the gates should never have been left open like this.

Yuan took a step toward the entrance and frowned when a powerful stench suddenly assaulted his nose—the unmistakable smell of death.

Ignoring the stench, Yuan walked through the entrance, followed a short passage, and arrived at an enclosed chamber.

The frown Yuan had worn since entering the chamber deepened when he saw the horrifying scene before him—one gruesome enough to disturb even the most cold-hearted killer.

Thousands of corpses were piled throughout the chamber, their bodies submerged in a pool of dried blood.

Although these corpses were burned beyond recognition, Yuan immediately knew they were the Heavenly White Tigers that had once lived there.

Yuan clenched his fists, his eyes flickering with anger.

Mu Xuelian, who was standing beside him, closed her eyes and sighed inwardly.

’Judging by the state of the corpses and the dried blood... this didn’t happen recently,’ Yuan thought.

A few minutes later, Yuan turned around and left.
